traits: Brown lizard doing push-ups and bobbing its head on walkways
Orange-red throat fan (dewlap) displayed by males
A smooth-edged crest along the neck, back, and tail in males
Ground and low-perch dweller, 5-9 inches total length

look_alikes.difference: Brown anoles stay brown-gray and low to the ground; green anoles can shift between green and brown and perch higher in shrubs.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the throat fan color while displaying, plus how high off the ground it is.

copy.what_it_means: An invasive lizard that has pushed Florida’s native green anole up into the trees — look up to find the green ones. It eats large numbers of insects and is the lanai’s volunteer security team; no treatment needed.
copy.fact: The invasive cousin — it pushed Florida’s native green anole up into the trees. Look up to find the green ones.
copy.blurb: Eats enormous numbers of insects. The lanai’s volunteer security team.

tech_notes: Beneficial insectivore; no treatment. Not a pest-control matter; educate if asked about population.

review.notes: A dedicated Featured Creatures page for Hemidactylus house geckos could not be reached during this pass (404/410 on the pages found); facts here reflect widely corroborated general knowledge and should be spot-checked against a live UF/IFAS gecko publication.

traits: Pale, almost translucent lizard active on walls at night
Clusters around porch lights hunting insects
Audible chirping and clicking calls in the evening
Toe pads that let it climb smooth vertical surfaces

look_alikes.difference: House geckos are pale, nocturnal, and cling to walls near lights; brown anoles are brown, active by day, and stay closer to the ground.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the skin color and whether it was seen by day or at night near a light.

copy.what_it_means: One of the few lizards with a voice — the evening chirps are territorial calls. It runs night-shift bug patrol around porch lights, and any droppings on the windowsill are simply the rent for that free pest control.
copy.fact: One of the few lizards with a voice — those evening chirps are territorial calls.
copy.blurb: Night-shift bug patrol. The droppings on the windowsill are the rent.

tech_notes: Beneficial insectivore; no treatment. Non-native Hemidactylus species are common and harmless around structures.
